title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: question-form wrapper bypasses the approval-synonym and command-execution checks
scenario: isSensitive() returns false as soon as QUESTION matches the normalized transcript (line 183), before the SYN_WINDOW, SYN_STANDALONE and EXEC checks run. QUESTION (line 87) is anchored on how|what|why|should|is|are|does|... so any imperative prefixed by one of those words skips the non-direct refusal rules. Verified by evaluating the delta's regexes: 'why dont you restart the server' is QUESTION=true, EXEC never runs, and the utterance routes to chat(). The same request without the wrapper, 'can you restart the server' or 'restart the server', is refused (EXEC matches 'restart\s+\S'). Other examples that reach chat: 'should you accept the pending request' (SYN 'accept'+'request' skipped), 'how about you install the package', 'is it okay to ratify the request' (ratify is only in SYN_VERB), 'should you unlock it'. Only direct verbs in SENSITIVE[0..] (approve, allow, grant, delete, push, etc.) still refuse in question form.
fix: Do not let QUESTION skip the EXEC and SYN_WINDOW checks when the approval verb or command verb is imperative in a question wrapper ('should you', 'why don't you', 'how about you', 'is it okay to'). Exempt only the 'how do I / what does X mean / explain' forms, or require the target to be an approval-like noun before exempting. Add classifier tests for 'why dont you restart the server', 'should you accept the pending request' and 'how about you install the package'.
why: Confirmed at HEAD ae026b1, src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-intent.ts. The QUESTION gate is new in this delta (git diff b80fab6 ae026b1 adds `const QUESTION` at line ~87 and `if (QUESTION.test(normalized)) return false;` inside isSensitive() before the SYN_WINDOW, SYN_STANDALONE and EXEC checks). Line 224 also skips the raw-text isSensitive check when QUESTION matches, and line 223's redirect refusal is skipped too. So any utterance starting with how|what|why|should|is|are|does|... that is an imperative skips every non-direct refusal rule. Regex evaluation of the delta's sources: "why dont you restart the server" gives QUESTION=true and EXEC=true but EXEC is never consulted; "should you accept the pending request" gives QUESTION=true and SYN_WINDOW matches but is never consulted; "is it okay to ratify the request" is QUESTION=true with no synonym match. Only the direct SENSITIVE[0..] verbs (approve, allow, grant, delete, push, etc.) still refuse in question form. The test added for question forms (voice-intent.test.ts line ~215) covers only plain questions ("how do I enable it", "should I accept it?") and no imperative wrappers, so the gap is untested. Routing: these fall through to make("chat") (line 246), which is tool-free and cannot execute or change approval state, so no execution authority is granted. The defect is that a sensitive request gets a spoken model answer instead of REFUSAL_TEXT, which breaks the "sensitive requests refused by voice" invariant for these wrappers. That is a limited defense and truthfulness gap, hence MEDIUM rather than HIGH. The claim's examples are accurate.

CONFIRMED (real=true, MEDIUM). FIX-INCOMPLETE: question-form wrapper bypasses the approval-synonym and command-execution checks. Read at HEAD ae026b1, src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-intent.ts.

Evidence:
- QUESTION (line ~87) is anchored on how|what|why|should|is|are|does|... and is introduced by this delta. b80fab6 has no QUESTION constant; the guard is new in ae026b1 (fixcheck#4).
- isSensitive() (lines ~180-188): SENSITIVE direct verbs run first, then `if (QUESTION.test(normalized)) return false;` runs BEFORE SYN_WINDOW, SYN_STANDALONE, EXEC and the CANCEL_OBJECT check. So any QUESTION-prefixed utterance skips those four families.
- classifyTranscript (~line 224): `isSensitive(normalized) || (!QUESTION.test(normalized) && isSensitive(raw))`. For a QUESTION-prefixed transcript the raw re-check is also skipped, so there is no second chance. The REDIRECT check is also gated on !QUESTION.
- Traced "why dont you restart the server": normalizeTranscript leaves "why" in place, QUESTION=true, EXEC never runs, no other branch matches, result kind "chat". The same request without the wrapper ("restart the server") matches EXEC `restart\s+\S` and is sensitive_refused.
- "should you accept the pending request" (SYN_VERB accept + target request, no direct verb): QUESTION skips the synonym check, result "chat". "is it okay to ratify the request" and "should you unlock it" behave the same way.
- voice-session.server.ts dispatch(): "chat" goes to chat() (~line 840-865), which is tool-free and admitted only when waiting_for_approval/mayLaunch. Otherwise it speaks TOOLS_TEXT. The spoken answer is a model reply, not REFUSAL_TEXT, and the sensitive_refused branch that opens the approvals surface (setUi("open_approvals")) is not reached.
- SPOKEN_CHAT_INSTRUCTION (lines 38-43) forbids claiming action, so no execution, no approval state change and no proposal is created. The impact is limited to the sensitive-refused invariant and truthfulness of the spoken answer and UI, which matches MEDIUM rather than HIGH or BLOCKER.

Refutation attempts that failed: direct verbs in SENSITIVE (approve, allow, grant, delete, push, delegate, scope, etc.) still refuse in question form, so the gap is limited to the synonym, EXEC and CANCEL-object families as the claim says. The bypass is therefore not a no-op. The claim's line numbers are approximately right (the early return is at ~183). The suggested fix (do not let QUESTION skip EXEC/SYN for imperative wrappers, and add classifier tests) is appropriate.

title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: command-execution list still omits start, so 'start the server' routes to chat
scenario: The round-2 authz#1 fix asked for imperative execution verbs with or without a noun, including start. The EXEC verb list (run|execute|launch|install|uninstall|restart|reboot|shut down|power off|download|spawn|invoke) has no start, and the older SENSITIVE[2] rule (line 46) needs a listed noun such as command, script, code, terminal, npm or git. 'start the server', 'start the build' and 'kick off the build' therefore match no sensitive rule, fall through to chat(), and the tool-free model can answer as if the server started. 'ship it' is also not in any approval or execution list and reaches chat.
fix: Add start|starts|starting to the EXEC verb list with an object-agnostic rule, or with a machine or project object (server, build, app, service, process, tests). Add 'ship it' to the approval or execution rules. Add R2-authz#1 tests for 'start the server', 'start the build' and 'ship it'.
why:
FIX-INCOMPLETE: command-execution list still omits start, so "start the server" routes to chat. Verified by reading HEAD (ae026b1) src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-intent.ts, read-only.

- EXEC list (lines 90-97) has run|execute|launch|install|uninstall|restart|reboot|shut down|power off|download|spawn|invoke. It has no start. The round-2 authz#1 finding in test-results/ma3/t10/review/round2-findings.json explicitly asked for start, so the delta does not implement what was requested.
- SENSITIVE[2] (line 46) only fires with a listed noun (command, script, code, terminal, npm, git, ...). "server", "build" and "app" are not listed, so "start the server" and "start the build" match nothing.
- Hand trace: "start the server", "start the build" and "kick off the build" match no REDIRECT, SENSITIVE, SYN, EXEC, CANCEL, CONTROL, STATUS or other rule. classifyTranscript falls through to make("chat") at the end of the function.
- voice-intent.test.ts R2-authz#1 (line 228-231) covers run/restart/kill/install/reboot/shut down/download/format/build but has no start case. grep finds no start test except "start a new mission".
- Impact is bounded. chat() is tool-free, and SPOKEN_CHAT_INSTRUCTION (voice-session.server.ts:38-43) forbids claiming action. The risk is a refusal gap plus a possible spoken false claim, which is a truthfulness and limited-defense defect, so MEDIUM fits.
- "ship it" is weaker. It was not in the requested authz#1 verb list, so I do not count it as a defect of this delta. The start gap alone is sufficient.

FIX-INCOMPLETE: confirmed at HEAD ae026b1, src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-intent.ts. The round-2 finding "Command-execution requests without a listed noun route to the tool-free chat model" (test-results/ma3/t10/review/round2-findings.json, authz lens) explicitly asks for `start` in its fix text ("run, execute, restart, kill, install, reboot, build, test, deploy, start..."). The delta's EXEC list (lines 90-97) has run|execute|launch|install|uninstall|restart|reboot|shut down|power off|download|spawn|invoke, with no start. SENSITIVE[2] (line 46) still requires a listed noun (command, script, code, terminal, npm, git, ...), and "server", "build" and "app" are not in it. I traced "start the server", "start the build" and "kick off the build" through classifyTranscript: none matches SENSITIVE, EXEC, REDIRECT, CONTROL, STATUS or the others, so each returns make("chat") at line 246. The chat path is tool-free (chat() at voice-session.server.ts:~845) and SPOKEN_CHAT_INSTRUCTION forbids claiming any action, so the impact is a refusal gap plus a model-dependent truthfulness risk, not an execution path. That is the same class as the round-2 MEDIUM, so MEDIUM is consistent. The "ship it" part is weaker: it is not in any round-2 finding, and "ship" is not an execution verb in the code, so it is only a suggestion and not a demonstrated invariant break. The main claim holds on the start omission alone. Lines in the claim are accurate (EXEC at 90-97, SENSITIVE noun list at 46).

title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: approval idioms 'give the green light', 'greenlit it' and 'you have my approval' still route to chat
scenario: The round-2 truth#3 fix adds green-light forms only as SYN_VERB entries that need an approval-like target within 30 characters, and SYN_STANDALONE covers only 'make it so', 'go for it', 'I consent', 'sign it off', 'give the go-ahead' and ok/fine + target. 'give the green light' has no target and no standalone rule, so it is not refused. 'greenlit it' is not matched because the regex has greenlight(ed)? and green[- ]?light(ed|ing|s)? but not the past tense 'greenlit'. 'you have my approval' and 'I give my approval' have an approval noun but no approval verb. All three reach chat(), where the model may answer 'approved' or 'done'.
fix: Add 'greenlit' and the bare 'green light' idiom (with 'give/have/got the') to SYN_STANDALONE. Add approval-noun possession forms ('have my approval', 'give my approval', 'got the green light', 'approval is given') to the refusal rules. Add classifier tests for each phrasing with and without a pending proposal.
why: Claim as stated does not hold exactly. I ran classifyTranscript from voice-intent.ts at HEAD (ae026b1) with proposalPending false and true. Results: "give the green light" -> chat (both). "greenlit it" -> chat (both). "you have my approval" -> agent_approvals, not chat, because the APPROVALS rule /\b(any|my) approvals?\b/ (voice-intent.ts ~line 141, checked at ~line 237) matches before the fall-through. "I give my approval" -> agent_approvals too. So one of the three named phrasings is misrouted in the claim, and the claimed "reaches chat" for approval-noun possession forms is wrong. The substantive gap is real and narrower: "give the green light" and "greenlit it" (and also "got the green light" and "approval is given", which the claim omits) fall through to make("chat") at line ~246 and dispatch to chat() (voice-session.server.ts ~687). Severity MEDIUM is appropriate for the narrowed defect: chat is tool-free, SPOKEN_CHAT_INSTRUCTION forbids claiming approval, and no execution, approval or identity authority is granted, so the impact is a missed refusal and a possible misleading spoken answer. Suggested corrected title: "FIX-INCOMPLETE: 'give the green light', 'greenlit it' and 'approval is given' still route to chat". The 'you have my approval' example should be dropped or re-scoped as a misroute to the approvals listing, which is read-only and not a grant.

Claim as filed does not hold exactly; read-only trace of src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-intent.ts at HEAD (ae026b1).

Refuted parts:
- "you have my approval" and "I give my approval" do not reach chat(). APPROVALS (voice-intent.ts line 141) contains /\b(any|my) approvals?\b/, which matches "my approval". classifyTranscript returns make("agent_approvals") (line 237), and voice-session.server.ts dispatch (lines 683-684) answers with the host_facts approvals listing (answerApprovals), not chat(). The claim's routing statement for these two phrasings is wrong. This route is read-only, so no execution or approval authority is involved.

Confirmed parts:
- "give the green light" reaches chat(). SYN_VERB matches "green light", but SYN_WINDOW needs an SYN_TARGET within 30 characters and there is none. SYN_STANDALONE has no bare green-light rule and no "give the green light" form. CONTROL, STATUS, VERIFY (line 133 needs have/did plus a test word) and REDIRECT do not match. Result: "chat".
- "greenlit it" reaches chat(). The alternation is greenlight(ed)?, which does not match "greenlit". SYN_WINDOW needs a verb after the target "it", and there is none. Result: "chat".

So a narrower defect holds: two of the three listed phrasings ("give the green light", "greenlit it") are a missing refusal that reaches the tool-free chat model. Impact is limited to a spoken model answer with no host action, which is the same class the round-1 and round-2 findings rated MEDIUM. The claim as written, which says all three reach chat, is not real, so real=false. If re-filed narrowed to those two phrasings, it would be MEDIUM with a FIX-INCOMPLETE prefix. Suggested fix: add "greenlit" and a bare "give the green light" form to SYN_STANDALONE, and add classifier tests (test file has a round-2 truth#3 test at voice-intent.test.ts line 265, but no entry for these two phrasings).

title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: idiom rule over-refuses ordinary acknowledgements and agent control
scenario: SYN_STANDALONE's last pattern (line 83) is not anchored and ends in \b, so any 'ok/okay/alright/all right/fine' followed by optional 'to/with' and then 'it', 'this one', 'the agent', 'the tool' or 'the command' is refused. It runs on both the normalized transcript and the raw transcript. Legitimate chat and control are refused: 'okay, the agent is paused' (status), 'that is fine, it is working now' (acknowledgement), 'okay, it looks great', and 'ok the agent, pause it' (control). The refusal replaces the pause control with REFUSAL_TEXT. The raw check does not run for questions, so these refusals hit non-question utterances.
fix: Anchor the standalone idiom to the whole utterance, for example ^(?:ok|okay|alright|fine)(?:,?\s+(?:to|with))?\s+(?:it|them|this one|the request|the approval|the agent|the tool|the command)$ with the target as the only remaining text, or require the approval verb (give/grant/okay to) rather than a bare acknowledgement. Add tests for 'okay, it looks great', 'okay, the agent is paused' (agent_status) and 'ok the agent, pause it' (agent_control).
why:
Claim holds at HEAD ae026b1. FIX-INCOMPLETE: the over-refusal defect is in code added by this delta.

Evidence:
- voice-intent.ts:83 (SYN_STANDALONE, added in ae026b1 per `git diff b80fab6 ae026b1`) is an unanchored regex ending in \b: /\b(?:ok|okay|alright|all right|fine)(?:[\s,]+(?:to|with))?[\s,]+(?:it|them|those|these|this one|the request|the approval|the agent|the tool|the command)\b/.
- Node test of that exact regex on the raw wording: "okay, the agent is paused" true; "that is fine, it is working now" true; "okay, it looks great" true; "ok the agent, pause it" true; control cases "okay that's great, thanks" and "okay, one more thing about the poem" false.
- Trace through classifyTranscript: for "okay, the agent is paused" the normalized form "the agent is paused" matches nothing sensitive, but line 224 runs isSensitive(raw) for non-questions, and raw matches line 83, so kind = sensitive_refused. The same happens to "okay, it looks great" and "ok the agent, pause it" (the latter loses its pause control). Status and control branches are never reached.
- The session maps sensitive_refused to REFUSAL_TEXT (voice-session.server.ts:45, :652), so the user hears "I can't do that by voice" for benign speech.

Impact: over-refusal only. No execution, approval or identity authority changes, and the refusal is truthful about the outcome. Screen controls remain. Severity LOW matches the claim. The claim's test-coverage remark is accurate in substance (no test covers "okay, it ..." or "okay the agent ..."), though I did not weigh it into severity.

Claim confirmed at HEAD ae026b1, voice-intent.ts. Line 83 (the last SYN_STANDALONE pattern) is new in this delta, since the diff from b80fab6 adds SYN_STANDALONE. It is unanchored, starts with a leading \b, and ends in \b. isSensitive() runs on the normalized text, and classifyTranscript line 224 also runs isSensitive(raw) for non-question utterances, so the raw form is checked too. Node evaluation of the exact regex: "okay, the agent is paused" -> true, "that is fine, it is working now" -> true, "okay, it looks great" -> true, "ok the agent, pause it" -> true on the raw form, "okay the tool is slow" -> true. Refusals for "okay, the agent is paused" and "okay, the agent" are reached before STATUS/CONTROL, so they return sensitive_refused. Control and status are lost for these phrasings. Controls: "okay that's great, thanks" and "okay, one more thing about the poem" stay chat, as the existing test covers. No execution, approval or identity authority changes, and no invariant is broken beyond over-refusal (the refusal is the safe direction). The defect is real but limited to usability and control availability, so LOW fits.

title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: 'cancel the pending pause' is refused as a sensitive command
scenario: CANCEL_OK_OBJECT allows only 'cancel [the|my|this|that] proposal|pause|confirmation|it|that|this|please|now'. 'cancel the pending pause' and 'cancel the pending proposal' fail that check, so isSensitive() treats the utterance as an object cancel (CANCEL_OBJECT with stopRest null) and returns sensitive_refused. The user is cancelling a pending pause, which the round-2 authz#2 fix intended to be a plain cancel. The refusal also opens the approvals surface when approvals exist.
fix: Allow an optional adjective before the object in CANCEL_OK_OBJECT ('(?:(?:the|my|this|that)\s+)?(?:(?:pending|current|active)\s+)?(?:proposal|pause|confirmation|...)'), and add a test for 'cancel the pending pause' with a proposal pending returning cancel.
why: The mechanism is real but the claim does not hold as a round-2 FIX-INCOMPLETE. Verified at HEAD (ae026b1) voice-intent.ts: CANCEL_OK_OBJECT (line 104) has no optional adjective, so "cancel the pending pause" and "cancel the pending proposal" fail CANCEL_OK_OBJECT, and isSensitive() returns true via CANCEL_OBJECT && !CANCEL_OK_OBJECT && stopRest===null (line 187). Node evaluation confirmed this (CANCEL_OBJ=true, OK_OBJ=false, stopRest null). The claim's premise that the round-2 authz#2 fix intended this to be a plain cancel is unsupported: test-results/ma3/t10/review/round2-findings.json contains no finding about "cancel the pending pause", and the delta's own test (voice-intent.test.ts:248) deliberately asserts that other cancel objects are sensitive_refused. The CANCEL regex (line 119) also does not accept "pending", so even with the sensitive branch removed the utterance would not be a cancel; it would fall through to chat. The result is a fail-closed over-refusal on a benign phrasing with no authority change, which is a design-gap at most and does not meet the bar of a concrete round-2 fix defect or an invariant break. Not reported as a defect of this delta.

FIX-INCOMPLETE: 'cancel the pending pause' is refused as sensitive_refused; claim confirmed at HEAD (ae026b1). Evidence: (1) src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-intent.ts:104 CANCEL_OK_OBJECT = /^(?:cancel|abort|kill|terminate)\s+(?:(?:the|my|this|that)\s+)?(?:proposal|pause|confirmation|it|that|this|please|now)\b/ does not match "cancel the pending pause" because "pending" is not in the list. (2) isSensitive (lines 181-188) reaches line 187: CANCEL_OBJECT matches, CANCEL_OK_OBJECT does not, and stopRest returns null, so it returns true. (3) classifyTranscript line 224 then returns sensitive_refused, and voice-session.server.ts:650-652 speaks REFUSAL_TEXT and sets open_approvals when approvals exist. The claim's suggested fix is incomplete, though. Even if the sensitivity check passed, CANCEL at line 119 (cancel(?:\s+(?:it|that|this|please|now|the (?:proposal|pause|confirmation)))*\s*$) also rejects "cancel the pending pause", so the utterance would fall through to chat or redirect, not cancel. Both regexes need the optional adjective. The delta introduced this over-refusal: before ae026b1, CANCEL was ^cancel\b and matched it as cancel. Impact is fail-closed over-refusal with no authority change, so LOW holds. No test covers it: voice-intent.test.ts:244-248 only covers "cancel the proposal" with a proposal pending and "cancel the upload".

title: Consent-pending agent hidden from spoken approvals when its Mission has any unrelated unresolved request
scenario: pendingApprovalFacts skips an agent whenever agent.missionId is in missionsAsking (any unresolved mission permission request). The agent's canonical consent offer (authorization.state WAITING_FOR_USER, a separate store from mission.requests) is then dropped without checking that the request is the same ask. Mission M has an unresolved permission request R1 and agent A on M has consent WAITING_FOR_USER. Facts count one item (R1) and the spoken approvals answer says one thing waits, while the Windows screen shows A as Needs approval. The same consent wait is not counted.
fix: Dedupe only when the consent offer's identity matches the request (or count consent independently), and add a test with a consent-pending agent on a mission that also has an unrelated unresolved request.
why:
Claim holds at HEAD ae026b1. The dedupe was introduced by this delta (T10-SUP#3), so it is in scope.

Evidence:
- src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-answers.server.ts:149 (`if (agent.missionId && missionsAsking.has(agent.missionId)) continue;`) runs before the consentPending check on the next line. missionsAsking is keyed only by mission.id and filled from any unresolved mission.requests entry.
- Consent is a separate canonical state. agentic-store.server.ts (src/lib/bunny-missions) sets current_state WAITING_FOR_USER on propose (line 88) and on host restart for ACTIVE/PAUSED envelopes (line 43). projection.pending (line 165) is the mission's unresolved requests, a different store. Nothing ties the consent offer to a specific request.
- Reachability: unresolved mission requests persist across restart (no restart-time resolution of plain step requests found), and restart forces consent back to WAITING_FOR_USER. So a mission can have both an unrelated unresolved request and a consent wait. Facts then count one item while the Windows screen (agent-model/workspace-model treat consent WAITING as Needs approval) shows the agent as waiting. The undercount persists until the request is resolved, and approving the request does not clear consent WAITING.
- Existing test voice-answers.test.ts (T10 H7 case) covers agent state WAITING_FOR_USER and mission requests separately, not a consent-pending agent on a mission with an open request. The gap is untested.

Impact is limited: the voice answer is informational, voice cannot approve, and the error self-corrects when the request resolves. That is a truthfulness gap, so MEDIUM fits. Not a round-2 fix, so no FIX-INCOMPLETE prefix.

Confirmed at HEAD ae026b1. voice-answers.server.ts:148-149 runs `if (agent.missionId && missionsAsking.has(agent.missionId)) continue;` before the consentPending check, and missionsAsking is keyed only by mission id. The consent offer is a separate per-mission envelope (src/lib/bunny-missions/agentic-store.server.ts:88 propose sets WAITING_FOR_USER; projection at :156-165 lists mission requests as `pending` separately from `state`), so the dedupe drops a distinct wait. No test covers a consent-pending agent on a mission with an unrelated unresolved request. The existing T10-SUP#3 test (voice-answers.test.ts ~line 160) has no authorization field on its agents, and the R2-truth#2 tests use missions: []. Reachability is plausible via agentic-store.server.ts:42-43, where an ACTIVE envelope from a prior Host generation is downgraded to WAITING_FOR_USER on restart while mission requests persist. I did not run it. Impact is a truthfulness undercount in the spoken approvals answer (one of two distinct asks is not counted), with no execution or authority effect, so MEDIUM fits. The dedupe was introduced by this delta, so the round-2 fix is over-broad; a title prefix of FIX-INCOMPLETE would be accurate, though the claim's own title omits it.

title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: bare 'cancel' while a name-choice clarification is pending is spoken as 'Nothing is waiting to be cancelled.'
scenario: A clarification is pending (two agents share a name). The user says 'cancel'. acceptFinal calls resolveClarification, which runs clearClarification() before pickCandidate fails, so both this.clarification and snap.clarification are nulled. dispatch('cancel') then computes pending = false and speaks 'Nothing is waiting to be cancelled.' The pending choice was in fact dropped, but the speech says nothing was waiting. The authz#2 fix was meant to make cancel speech truthful.
fix: Capture pending = proposal || clarification before resolveClarification runs (or let resolveClarification report that it consumed a clarification), and speak 'Okay, cancelled.' when a clarification was consumed by the cancel. Add a test for cancel with a pending clarification.
why: FIX-INCOMPLETE: the claim holds at HEAD ae026b1. A bare "cancel" while a name-choice clarification is pending traces as follows. acceptFinal (voice-session.server.ts ~568-569) classifies "cancel" as kind "cancel", which is not sensitive_refused, so resolveClarification runs. resolveClarification (~619-622) calls clearClarification() before pickCandidate("cancel", candidates), which returns null because "cancel" matches neither a candidate name nor an ordinal. It returns false, leaving this.clarification and snap.clarification both null. dispatch case "cancel" (~659) then computes pending = !!snap.proposal || !!snap.clarification, which is false, and speaks "Nothing is waiting to be cancelled." The pending choice was dropped, so the speech is untrue. No action executes, so the impact is a truthfulness defect, not an execution one. The pending line is new in ae026b1 (visible in git diff b80fab6 ae026b1), and it implements the round-2 finding "Spoken 'cancel' answers 'Okay, cancelled.' while the named agent keeps running", so this is an incomplete fix. Severity MEDIUM matches a limited truthfulness gap.

FIX-INCOMPLETE: bare "cancel" while a name-choice clarification is pending is spoken as "Nothing is waiting to be cancelled." The claim holds at HEAD (ae026b1). Trace: acceptFinal (voice-session.server.ts:565-569) runs classifyTranscript("cancel") -> kind "cancel" (voice-intent.ts:231, CANCEL regex at line 119). It is not sensitive, so it calls resolveClarification (line 569). That function calls clearClarification() (line 622), which nulls both this.clarification and snap.clarification. pickCandidate("cancel", candidates) returns null (no name match, no ordinal), so it returns false. dispatch("cancel") then computes pending = !!snap.proposal || !!snap.clarification at line 659 after the clear, so pending is false and the speech is "Nothing is waiting to be cancelled." (line 663). The pending choice was in fact dropped, so no control ran and state is safe, but the spoken state is false. The authz#2 fix in the delta is the line-663 branch, and it does not cover this path. The existing test at voice-session.test.ts:1332-1343 covers only a proposal and a bare cancel with nothing pending, so no test covers cancel with a pending clarification. Severity MEDIUM is right: a truthfulness gap in speech, with no execution or identity impact. The fix suggested in the claim is correct: capture pending before resolveClarification, or have it report that it consumed a clarification.

title: Second close() during an in-flight close can reopen the session and orphan a worker that keeps the microphone
scenario: close#1 has detached this.worker (worker A) and is awaiting worker.close(). close#2 arrives. The guard `!this.worker && !this.snap.open` passes because snap.open is still true, so close#2 runs synchronously through resetAfterClose() and sets snap.open=false. A new open() then runs startWorker, which sets this.worker = B and sets snap.open=true in doOpen. If B's open completes before close#1 resumes, close#1 runs resetAfterClose() again: snap.open=false, sessionId=null, while this.worker is still B. The snapshot says closed, the journal says 'microphone and speaker released', and B is live. The next open() overwrites this.worker with C and B is never closed. Its events are ignored because they fail the `this.worker === worker` check. The window is narrow and needs two close requests plus an open in between.
fix: Make close() idempotent with a shared in-flight promise (return the existing close promise while closing), and have startWorker refuse or close a worker already attached to this.worker.
why: The re-entry path is real but the claim as stated does not hold. Verified at HEAD: close() (voice-session.server.ts:303-331) detaches this.worker before awaiting worker.close(), and the guard at line 306 passes while snap.open is true, so a second close() can run resetAfterClose() during the first. A later open() can then set this.worker=B (startWorker line 258 does not close a previous worker), and the first close() resumes and resets snap.open=false while B is live. Two gaps undercut the claim. (1) "Keeps the microphone" is wrong: the worker opens devices only on capture.start (voice-session capture.start at line 398; protocol says capture.started means real device open). Once snap.open is false, listenStart and text refuse (snap.open / !this.worker checks), and this.worker is later replaced by C, so B never receives a capture or speak command and holds no mic or speaker. (2) The orphaned process is still inside its OwnedProcessGroup job, so it is contained, not uncontained. The residual defect is an idle leaked contained worker process plus a snapshot/process mismatch, which needs two close requests and an open inside the up-to-2s graceful shutdown window (worker close() waits shutdownGraceMs=2000). That is LOW hardening, not MEDIUM. The guard and worker-detach ordering predate the delta (line 306 and the detach were already in b80fab6), and the delta does not touch the open() path, so it is not a round-2 fix defect and it is not in round2-findings.json. Given the claim's mechanism is partly wrong and the impact is overstated, real=false with a LOW residual.

Claim holds at HEAD ae026b1 as a real, narrow race. Suggested title for the report: "FIX-INCOMPLETE: second close() during an in-flight close resets the races#3 closing gate and can reopen over a live worker".

Verified in voice-session.server.ts at HEAD:
- close() (lines 303-331): the guard at line 306 is `!this.worker && !this.snap.open`. While close#1 awaits worker.close() (line 326), this.worker is already null (line 322) but snap.open is still true, so close#2 passes the guard. With no inference, close#2 has no await before resetAfterClose() (line 327), so it sets snap.open=false synchronously and sets closing=false (line 328) while close#1 is still in flight.
- open() (lines 195-208) has no closing check and no re-entry guard on an in-flight close. With snap.open=false it calls doOpen, which calls startWorker (line 258 `this.worker = worker`, with no close of any previous worker) and then sets snap.open=true (line 229).
- If B's doOpen completes before close#1 resumes, close#1 runs resetAfterClose() again (sessionId=null, snap.open=false, while this.worker is still B), then journals "microphone and speaker released" (line 329). B stays live and this.worker is overwritten by the next open. Its exit handler returns early at line 1188 (worker !== this.worker), so B is never closed by the manager. Only Windows job kill-on-close at host exit would end it.
- Requests are not serialized: http.server.ts voiceCommand (lines 1138-1155) dispatches voice.session.close and voice.session.open directly, so two concurrent requests from the local workstation principal reach the manager.

Refutation attempts that did not succeed: the window is not infinite. close#1 must still be in worker.close() (graceful exit up to shutdownGraceMs, voice-worker.server.ts 255-270) when B finishes launch plus ready. If A exits first, close#1 resets before B's doOpen and no defect remains. So the window is timing-dependent. It is also not reachable remotely: voice actions are workstation-only (http.server.ts line 631 refuses device principals).

Pre-existing check: the detach-then-await order at b80fab6 (lines 321-326) is the same, so the race predates the delta. The delta is still in scope because it introduced the boolean `closing` gate that the round-2 races#3 finding asked for (a closed flag that refuses listenStart and text while closing). A second close resets that boolean to false early (line 328) while the first close is still running, so the round-2 fix is incomplete for this path. That is why the FIX-INCOMPLETE prefix is used.

Severity MEDIUM: a microphone can stay live while the snapshot and journal say it is closed (UI-truthfulness and "worker contained" gap). Impact is limited to a local double-close plus an open inside a short timing window, with job containment as a backstop. The claim's fix (a shared in-flight close promise, and startWorker refusing or closing a worker already attached to this.worker) is sound.

title: Low-confidence finals between 0.15 and 0.4 are still routed to chat and can run cancel, despite the 'never routed / never control' rule
scenario: A final with confidence 0.2 (above minFinalConfidence 0.15, below minControlConfidence 0.4) passes acceptFinal's first gate. Only confirm and agent_control are blocked below 0.4. A misheard utterance can still reach chat(), which speaks a model answer built from the misheard text, and 'cancel' still clears a pending proposal or clarification. Nothing executes an agent command, so the impact is a misleading spoken answer and an unexpected cancel.
fix: Route any final below minControlConfidence only to a fixed 'not sure, say it again' reply, and never to chat or cancel, or document 0.15 as the routing floor and add tests that pin both thresholds.
why: Refuted as a round-2 defect. The code facts in the claim are accurate: at ae026b1, voice-session.server.ts:553 gates only below minFinalConfidence (0.15), and lines 559 and 570 gate only clarification resolution and agent_control/confirm below minControlConfidence (0.4). A final at 0.2 therefore reaches chat() (line 688) and cancel (lines 657-664) with no confidence check. However: (1) the delta does not touch these lines (git diff b80fab6 ae026b1 shows no change to the gating), and it is not a round-2 finding in test-results/ma3/t10/review/round2-findings.json, so it is not an incomplete round-2 fix. (2) The two-threshold split is deliberate and documented at voice-protocol.ts:246-249: 0.15 is the "not heard, nothing is routed" floor and 0.4 is the control floor. Under that documented design, "low-confidence finals never routed" maps to the 0.15 floor, so the code does not break the stated invariant. (3) Impact is bounded even on the claim's own reading. Cancel only clears voice-side proposal/clarification state (screen-only, re-proposable). It never reaches agent.* controls, and it does not execute anything. Chat is tool-free local Ollama and speaks a model answer, with no execution or identity authority. A misheard spoken answer is at most a hardening note, not an invariant break introduced or left by this delta. Not reported.

Refuted as a defect introduced or left by the round-2 delta (b80fab6..ae026b1).

Facts in the claim check out at HEAD: voice-protocol.ts:247-249 sets minFinalConfidence 0.15 and minControlConfidence 0.4; voice-session.server.ts:553 gates only below 0.15; lines 559-561 and 570-574 block only agent_control and confirm below 0.4 (and clarification resolution while a clarification is pending); the chat dispatch (line 687) and cancel dispatch (line 657) have no confidence check. voice-protocol.ts is not in the delta's file list, so the thresholds and this routing are unchanged.

Why it does not hold as a defect:
- The code documents minFinalConfidence as the "not heard" floor: below it, nothing is routed. Between 0.15 and 0.4 the turn is routed, but the code's own minControlConfidence comment limits only agent controls and spoken confirmations. The implementation matches its stated design. The claim's "never routed" reading comes from the task's wording, not from a threshold the code defines.
- chat() is tool-free and local-only, so a misheard final yields at most a spoken answer to a misheard question. No agent command executes.
- cancel is not an agent.* control. It only clears a pending voice proposal or clarification, which is the fail-safe direction, and it executes nothing.
- No round-2 finding (round2-findings.json) covers this threshold, so the delta neither claims to fix it nor breaks a fix. It is a pre-existing design choice, not a FIX-INCOMPLETE.
At most this is a threshold-documentation or design-clarity point, which is below the LOW hardening bar this review is scoped to report. The suggested fix is a behavior change, not a repair of a broken round-2 fix.

title: Chat prompt history is concatenated without escaping, so a typed turn can forge prior User/Assistant lines
scenario: text() accepts up to 2000 characters, including newlines, and only trims them. chat() joins history as `User: ...\nAssistant: ...` without escaping, and the typed transcript is stored as the next turn's user text. One typed turn containing a newline followed by 'Assistant: ...' forges a prior assistant line in every later prompt. SPOKEN_CHAT_INSTRUCTION is advisory text that only the model can see. The forged text can steer the spoken answer (for example, 'I approved it') without any host action. The author is the paired device user, so the impact is limited to that user's own spoken answers.
fix: Collapse newlines and strip role markers from user and assistant text before building the prompt, or pass history as structured messages instead of one string. Add a test with an embedded 'Assistant:' line.
why: Claim refuted at HEAD (ae026b1). The history join in chat() (voice-session.server.ts ~846-852) and text() trim-only handling are real and unescaped, but the claim does not show a defect this delta introduced or left in a way that breaks an invariant. (1) The delta does not touch the history/prompt code: `git diff b80fab6 ae026b1` shows no changes to the history map, join, or prompt array; the delta only added SPOKEN_CHAT_INSTRUCTION as defense in depth. (2) Typed text comes from the paired device user, the same user who can already type any request. A forged "Assistant: I approved it" line grants no capability the user lacks: they could type "say I approved it" directly, and the chat path is tool-free and admitted only when task.mayLaunch and no mission, so no host action, approval, or agent control can follow from model text. (3) No identity, sensitive-request, or execution-authority invariant is crossed; speech is not involved (text() is the typed fallback). (4) The impact is a model-generated spoken sentence that the same user authored, which at most is a self-directed truthfulness wobble in an answer labeled as model output. That is hardening at most, and the report rules exclude nits and hardening without concrete invariant breach. The claimed line numbers are also slightly off (the map/join is at 846-851, not 850), though that is minor.

Claim refuted as a defect. Verified at HEAD ae026b1 in src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-session.server.ts: text() (around lines 465-470) only trims, so a typed turn can contain newlines, and chat() (lines 846-853) joins history as "User: ...\nAssistant: ..." without escaping. The newline-forgery mechanism exists as described. Its impact does not cross a trust boundary. (1) The only author of typed text is the paired device user, who can already type "say I approved it" directly, so the forged lines grant no capability the user lacked. (2) Forged history only feeds the tool-free local chat prompt. The chat() route admits only tool-free Ollama tasks (line ~876, state must be waiting_for_approval, hasMission false, mayLaunch true). It cannot approve, execute, or control agents. (3) Spoken finals reach acceptFinal (line ~546) without a newline-producing path, so the forgery requires typed input. (4) The delta does not touch this code path. SPOKEN_CHAT_INSTRUCTION is pre-existing and the join is unchanged in ae026b1 (the only prompt-related hunk is the instruction constant being added). The claim also cites line 850 where the join is at 848, a minor citation error. Residual, not a defect of this delta: model-generated answers are stored verbatim (answer.slice(0,600), line ~936) and could carry newlines into later prompts, but that is model output from the same user's session with no authority attached. Empty findings list is the correct result.

title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: WaveIn buffers are zeroed and freed without checking the driver still owns them
scenario: WaveInSource.Close() (lines 683-702) calls waveInReset, waveInUnprepareHeader and waveInClose and ignores every return code, sets handle to zero, then runs WipeNative and FreeHGlobal on each data buffer. The new comment on line 695 says 'the device is reset and the headers unprepared above, so no driver write can race the wipe', but nothing checks that. If the driver still holds a buffer (unprepare returns WAVERR_STILLPLAYING, or waveInClose fails), the wipe races a live DMA write and FreeHGlobal then leaves the driver writing into freed heap. The WaveOut side of this same delta keeps buffers on WAVERR_STILLPLAYING, so the two paths now handle the same driver contract differently. Pre-existing free behavior is unchanged, but the zeroing fix asserts a guarantee the code does not enforce.
fix: Check the waveInUnprepareHeader and waveInClose results. Keep (do not free or wipe) any buffer whose unprepare returns a still-in-use error, as WaveOut.Release does, and correct the comment so it does not claim a no-race guarantee the code does not check.
why: Refuted as a concrete defect. The code facts in the claim are accurate: BunnyVoiceWorker.cs WaveInSource.Close() (lines 683-705 at HEAD ae026b1) ignores the return codes of waveInReset, waveInUnprepareHeader and waveInClose, and WipeNative runs before FreeHGlobal on each data buffer. But the ordering rests on the documented waveInReset contract: waveInReset marks all pending buffers done and returns them to the application before it returns, so the driver owns no buffer once the reset succeeds. The claimed trigger (unprepare returns WAVERR_STILLPLAYING) therefore needs a driver that violates that contract, or a reset that fails silently while buffers are still queued. The claim itself concedes the trigger "contradicts the documented contract", and no evidence in the repo shows that path happening. The WaveOut contrast is also weaker than stated: WaveOut.Release (line 830) is per-chunk during playback, and WaveOut.Close (lines 855-870) also skips freeing on WAVERR_STILLPLAYING, so the two Close paths differ only in whether they keep a buffer, which is a hardening choice, not a proven invariant break. Residual: the zero-check and the stale comment are a LOW hardening gap at most, not a finding that survives verification.

Refuted as a defect introduced or left by the round-2 delta.

Code at HEAD ae026b1 (native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs): WaveInSource.Close() calls waveInReset, then waveInUnprepareHeader per header, then waveInClose, with no return checks. Lines 695-703 zero each data buffer with WipeNative, then FreeHGlobal. The claim's description of this is accurate.

The claim's trigger does not hold on the documented contract. waveInReset is documented to stop input, mark all pending buffers done, and return them to the application before it returns. After a successful reset no waveIn buffer is queued, so waveInUnprepareHeader should not return WAVERR_STILLPLAYING, and the new comment "no driver write can race the wipe" states the documented guarantee rather than a false one. The claim itself says the trigger needs a driver that violates that contract.

The only new behavior in the delta on this path is the zero-write before free. The free-under-live-DMA exposure the claim describes is pre-existing and unchanged by the delta. The zero-write adds no new memory-safety exposure. The WaveOut keep-on-STILLPLAYING asymmetry is a design difference, not a defect this delta introduced, since WaveOut has a documented still-playing return path that waveIn's reset-then-unprepare sequence does not produce. No concrete, reachable failure is evidenced, so this does not meet the bar for a reported finding even at LOW.

title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: WaveOut.Close still drops an open handle and abandons its chunks if the second waveOutClose fails
scenario: WaveOut.Close() (lines 855-872) retries waveOutClose once after a reset, ignores the second result, and sets handle to zero unconditionally. If both closes fail, the handle is leaked while still open. Any chunk skipped on WAVERR_STILLPLAYING is also cleared from submitted without being freed, so its header and PCM buffers are never reclaimed and the driver may still hold them. The round-2 finding on the timed-out chunk and waveOutClose failure is only partially fixed: the chunk-buffer leak is closed, but the handle and buffer leak remain for this path. No use-after-free results, because skipped chunks are not freed.
fix: Record a failed second close (for example, keep handle and the STILLPLAYING chunks in a retained list for a later retry or process exit), and make the comment state the actual outcome.
why: Verified at HEAD ae026b1, native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs WaveOut.Close (lines 855-872). The code matches the claim. After waveOutReset, the second waveOutClose result is ignored and handle = IntPtr.Zero runs unconditionally, so a double close failure leaks an open waveOut handle. The STILLPLAYING skip also drops chunks from `submitted` without FreeChunk, so their header and PCM memory is leaked. Neither is a use-after-free. The STILLPLAYING path is unlikely in practice because waveOutReset returns every pending header to the app before it returns, so the driver owns no chunk afterwards. The comment at lines 852-854 says the handle is closed even if the first close fails, which holds only when the retry succeeds. The round-2 finding "Timed-out playback chunk leaks its PCM and header buffers, and the device handle when waveOutClose fails" is therefore only partly fixed. The impact is a bounded resource leak on a shutdown or timeout path that process exit reclaims, which is LOW hardening. The claim's line numbers are close to HEAD, and the claim's severity and fix are reasonable.

Claim verified at HEAD ae026b1, native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs. Close() (about lines 855-872) calls waveOutReset, unprepares submitted headers and frees only those that do not return WAVERR_STILLPLAYING, clears submitted, then calls waveOutClose once. On a nonzero result it does one reset and one more waveOutClose, ignores that result, and sets handle to IntPtr.Zero unconditionally. If both closes fail, the open handle is dropped with no retry: CloseDevice() (about line 1975) nulls waveOut before and after Close, so nothing ever retries. The comment above Close ("the handle is closed even if the first waveOutClose fails") is only true when the retry succeeds. Skipped STILLPLAYING chunks are removed from submitted without FreeChunk, so their header and PCM buffers leak rather than being freed under a possibly live DMA read. The claim correctly says this is a leak, not a use-after-free. The round-2 finding "Timed-out playback chunk leaks its PCM and header buffers, and the device handle when waveOutClose fails" is therefore only partly addressed: the chunk leak on the normal path is closed, but the double-close-failure path still leaks the handle and buffers. Impact is bounded to a rare failure path in the playback worker, with no execution, identity, or consent impact, which fits LOW hardening. The title prefix FIX-INCOMPLETE: is accurate.

title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: captureBodyContained selftest passes without exercising the new capture-thread guard
scenario: ContainmentCheck runs CaptureTurn.StartCapture with LostSource (Read returns -1) and BrokenStream. With LostSource, CaptureLoop takes its own st < 0 branch, emits through Guard.Emit, calls Finish and breaks, so no exception ever reaches the Guard.Run wrapper or FaultCapture. Removing the Guard.Run wrapper from StartCapture would leave this check green. The check name 'captureBodyContained' therefore overstates what it verifies, and the containment fix's evidence is weaker than its claim.
fix: Use a source whose Read throws (or a seam that throws in CaptureLoop's try body outside its handlers) so the thread-level guard is the only catch, and assert that FaultCapture emitted capture.error and the thread ended.
why: Claim holds at HEAD ae026b1 (native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs). The production fix is in place: StartCapture (line ~1215) wraps CaptureLoop in Guard.Run with FaultCapture. The selftest ContainmentCheck (lines ~2357-2363) runs StartCapture(new LostSource()) with BrokenStream. LostSource.Read returns -1, so CaptureLoop takes its own st<0 branch. That branch calls EmitCaptureError (non-throwing, via Guard.Emit), Finish("error") (no throw on this thread) and break. The finally block only does Array.Clear, source.Close (wrapped), PublishOnset (lock, no I/O) and Guard.Emit. No exception escapes CaptureLoop, so removing the thread-level Guard.Run would leave captureBodyContained green. The claim's evidence is accurate and the check name overstates what it verifies. Refinement to the claim: its suggested remedy is only partly right. A Read that throws is caught by CaptureLoop's own catch(Exception) (about line 1337), so it would not reach the thread-level guard either. Only a fault inside that catch or the finally would escape to Guard.Run, and that path is currently unreachable from a test seam without new code. The defect is a test-evidence gap on a defense-in-depth guard, not an exploitable or invariant-breaking flaw, so LOW.

Confirmed at HEAD ae026b1 (native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs). The captureBodyContained check (around lines 2357-2363) runs CaptureTurn.StartCapture(new LostSource()). LostSource.Read returns -1, so CaptureLoop takes its own st < 0 branch (about line 1273): EmitCaptureError (wrapped in Guard.Emit, which never throws), Finish("error"), break. Nothing reaches the thread-level Guard.Run wrapper. The finally block (about lines 1345-1360) only calls Array.Clear, source.Close inside try/catch, PublishOnset, a lock, and Guard.Emit, so no exception escapes CaptureLoop either. The check therefore passes whether or not the Guard.Run wrapper at StartCapture (line 1215) exists, and the BrokenStream write failures are swallowed by Guard.Emit, so that part is not really exercised either. The name captureBodyContained overstates what is verified. The production wrapper itself is present and correct, so this is an evidence/test-strength gap rather than a runtime containment break. Severity LOW matches the hardening category. Claim line numbers are off by about one line (the StartCapture call is at 2359), which does not change the substance.

title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: Windows hotkey hold still sends source 'hotkey', so a held turn ends on VAD silence
scenario: User holds Ctrl+Alt+Space (Start-BunnyHotkeyHold) and pauses mid-sentence for about 1 s while the key stays down. Start-BunnyVoiceListen sends voice.listen.start with source 'hotkey'. The Host maps it to endpointing 'vad' (voice-session.server.ts:402 sets 'manual' only for source === 'push_to_talk'), so the Host ends the turn on silence while the key is still held. The Island's hold poll (Invoke-BunnyHotkeyPoll) only sends listen.end on release, and the 1.5 s stale-listening reset then clears the local flag, so the rest of the held utterance is not captured. The UI label stays truthful because it follows capture state, so this is a held-turn contract gap, not a false claim. Round-1 truth#3 asked for desktop hold-to-talk to use push_to_talk, and the delta fixed only the mouse path (Start-BunnyVoicePointer) and the web press path, not the hotkey hold.
fix: Send a hold-aware source on the hotkey hold path, for example start with 'push_to_talk' when the chord is held and keep VAD only for sub-350 ms taps (the hold/tap decision is known only at release, so the Host or the Island needs a source-upgrade or a re-endpoint rule). Add a Windows-side test or a Host test that a held hotkey turn is not VAD-ended while the chord is down.
why:
The claim holds on the code at HEAD (read-only; nothing run).

Mechanics confirmed:
- install/Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1 Start-BunnyHotkeyHold calls Start-BunnyVoiceListen 'hotkey' (no hold-aware source). The delta changes only the mouse path (Start-BunnyVoicePointer still sends 'push_to_talk'), not the hotkey path.
- http.server.ts:1139-1140 passes 'hotkey' through unchanged.
- voice-session.server.ts:402 sets endpointing to "manual" only for source === "push_to_talk"; 'hotkey' gets "vad".
- BunnyVoiceWorker.cs Vad uses SilenceEndMs = 900, and VadEndpoint turns finish with "vad" on speech_end. A held hotkey pause of about 1 s therefore ends the turn on the Host while the chord is still down.
- Invoke-BunnyHotkeyPoll sends listen.end only on release. Stop-BunnyVoiceListen is a no-op once the local flag is cleared by the 1.5 s stale-listening reset (line 362), so the rest of the held utterance is not captured.
- test-results/ma3/t10/voice-architecture.md:32 documents the chord as "hold, or tap with VAD end". The hold-with-VAD-end behaviour therefore contradicts the documented intent.

Severity judgement: this is a real held-turn contract gap and an incomplete round-2 fix (the hotkey hold path was not converted to push_to_talk). It does not break any listed invariant. Voice is not made an execution authority, no refusal or routing rule is bypassed, and no audio is retained or misreported. The UI label follows real capture state, so it stays truthful. That fits LOW (functional gap, no safety or truthfulness impact), matching the claim's own rating.

Claim holds at HEAD ae026b1; not refuted. Evidence chain checked:
- install/Bunny-Island.Voice.ps1:474-480: Start-BunnyHotkeyHold calls Start-BunnyVoiceListen 'hotkey' (line 478). Line 217 forwards source unchanged.
- http.server.ts:1139-1140: source() accepts 'hotkey' as-is.
- voice-session.server.ts:402: endpointing = source === "push_to_talk" ? "manual" : "vad", so 'hotkey' yields VAD endpointing.
- native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:995,1073: SilenceEndMs=900 and HypothesisHoldMs=700, so a ~1 s mid-sentence pause ends a VAD capture while the chord is still held.
- Island poll (lines 482-489) sends listen.end only on release. The 1.5 s stale reset at line 362 then clears the local flag, so the remainder of the held utterance is not captured.
- The delta (git diff b80fab6 ae026b1) touches Stop-BunnyVoiceHotkey and the web press path (src/components/island/voice-press.ts comment says hold-to-talk is manual), but not Start-BunnyHotkeyHold, so the round-1 truth#3 hotkey half remains unfixed. That makes it a FIX-INCOMPLETE.
- The UI label follows capture state, so there is no false claim. The impact is a held-turn contract gap, not an invariant break, which fits LOW.
Title prefix FIX-INCOMPLETE is correct for a round-2 finding that the delta left open.

title: Release turn binding is cleared after the await, so a concurrent press's turn can be unbound
scenario: Press 1 is released, so pressUp returns start 'none' plus listen_end. The store then awaits voice.listen.end bound to turn A (the await is up to 45 s on the command path). While it is in flight the user presses again, and listen_start completes with turn B, so pressTurn = B. When the listen.end for A returns, line 478 sets pressTurn = null, which clobbers B. The release for B is then sent unbound ({}), losing the Host's stale-turn guard. Impact is limited to unbound release semantics (the Host still ends the current capture), so this only matters if a third capture starts before B's release lands.
fix: Capture the bound turn before the await and clear only if pressTurn still equals that captured value (for example const bound = pressTurn; ...; if (pressTurn === bound) pressTurn = null;), or key the binding by a press sequence number. Add a store test that a listen.start resolving during a pending listen.end keeps its turn for the next release.
why:
Claim holds at HEAD ae026b1, with the title corrected to carry the FIX-INCOMPLETE prefix. The round-2 fix "A release binds to its own listen.start turn" is incomplete in this interleaving.

Evidence:
- src/store/use-island.ts:458 declares a single closure variable `let pressTurn`. Line 471 (`pressTurn = snapshot?.turnId ?? null`) is written by the listen_start branch. Line 477 reads it into the listen.end payload. Line 478 (`pressTurn = null`) runs after the await.
- The release path is not serialized against a new press. In src/components/island/voice-press.ts, pressUp from the `active` state moves to start `none` and emits listen_end. pressDown then accepts start `none` and emits a new listen_start (line 37). So press 2 can start while listen.end for turn A is still pending.
- If listen_start for B resolves before listen.end for A, pressTurn = B is set. When the A end resolves, line 478 sets pressTurn = null, clobbering B. The release for B then goes out as `{}`, unbound, which is the case the round-2 binding fix was meant to remove.

Why LOW: the unbound end still ends the Host's current capture, which is B in the normal sequence. The stale-turn guard only matters if a third capture starts between that unbound release and its arrival. That requires a stalled listen.end plus a rapid re-press. No invariant is broken by default. Line 478 is pre-existing, but the delta reworked this block and claimed to fix the binding, so the residual race counts against it.

Not verified: the Host-side handling of an unbound listen.end, and the exact COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS value. No tests or builds were run, per the read-only rule.

The race is real at HEAD ae026b1. In src/store/use-island.ts the listen.end branch reads pressTurn before the await (payload bound to turn A), then runs `pressTurn = null` after the await. voice-press.ts confirms the interleaving is reachable: pressUp on an active capture returns start "none" plus listen_end, and a new pressDown in that state returns start "in_flight" plus listen_start. Its runPress runs independently of A's pending end. So B's listen.start can resolve during A's listen.end, set pressTurn = B, and be clobbered to null when A's end returns. B's release then goes out as {} (unbound). The delta's own comment at the listen_start branch ("The release is bound to the turn this start was answered with") is therefore not upheld in this interleaving, so the defect is left by the delta, though the reset line itself predates it.

Severity is LOW, not higher. The unbound end still targets the only capture the Host holds (B's), and the Host's stale-turn guard only matters if a third capture starts before B's release is processed. No listed invariant (execution authority, identity, sensitive refusal, barge-in, raw audio, worker containment) is broken. The claim's suggested fix (capture the bound turn and clear only if pressTurn still equals it) is correct. Verified by reading HEAD code and the press state machine; I did not run tests.
